diagrams.title: From Existing Debt to Verified Retained Spread
diagrams.subtitle: Five linked controls separate a performing wrap from an opaque payment promise.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Workflow order is operational, not a forecast of five completed transactions. First-deal timing remains 2–6 months. Property value, loan principal, escrow deposits, and pass-through debt service are excluded from canonical operator revenue.
diagrams.caption: The operator acquires subject to existing debt without assuming that the original borrower has been released. A wrap adds a separate buyer obligation; it does not remove the senior lien.

stages.label: Source low-equity debt situations
stages.value: Match seller needs with verified existing debt
stages.detail: Use county recorder filings, foreclosure notices, and authorized seller records to identify low-equity situations. Confirm seller objectives, arrears, occupancy, and equity before pricing the existing rate advantage.

stages.label: Underwrite title and acceleration
stages.value: Price senior-lien exposure before making commitments
stages.detail: Obtain title work, mortgage statements, reinstatement figures, insurance terms, and the actual security instrument. Model lender acceleration under 12 U.S.C. §1701j-3 and reject transactions without a funded response.

stages.label: Qualify the wrap buyer
stages.value: Route every owner-occupant buyer through licensed origination
stages.detail: Have the licensed RMLO document income, assets, debts, credit obligations, and repayment capacity. Apply 12 CFR §1026.43 where covered and document the treatment of taxes, insurance, balloon terms, and payment changes.

stages.label: Close with transparent payment routing
stages.value: Execute recorded instruments and configure licensed servicing
stages.detail: Counsel and title professionals coordinate deed, wrap note, security instrument, notices, and lien priority. The licensed servicer establishes borrower autopay, underlying-payment routing, escrow handling, and reporting.

stages.label: Reconcile and manage exceptions
stages.value: Verify underlying payments before releasing retained cash
stages.detail: Reconcile the wrap ledger, underlying lender statement, bank settlement, tax account, and insurance evidence monthly. Escalate missing payments immediately; borrower autopay success alone does not prove senior-debt payment.

diagrams.title: One Cohort, Five Measurable Conversion Steps
diagrams.subtitle: A 500-record sourcing cohort narrows to six funded and boarded wraps.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative six-month cohort, not observed conversion data. Every stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Counts do not derive the $475,000 annual Base-Case revenue: annual retained interest also depends on the seasoned performing portfolio.
diagrams.caption: Track losses by reason: seller mismatch, title defects, acceleration liquidity, buyer repayment capacity, and closing attrition. Do not count an application as a funded wrap.

stages.label: Screened seller records
stages.value: 500 unique records establish the cohort denominator
stages.detail: Deduplicate property and owner records, verify the trigger date, and document contact eligibility. This starting population represents 100% of the defined cohort.

stages.label: Documented seller conversations
stages.value: 150 conversations equal 30% of screened records
stages.detail: Count only sellers who discuss debt terms and transaction objectives. The remaining 350 records never advance into documented underwriting during this cohort window.

stages.label: Debt-and-title qualified opportunities
stages.value: 45 opportunities equal 30% of seller conversations
stages.detail: Require usable debt evidence, preliminary title findings, a priceable arrears position, and a credible acceleration response. These opportunities equal 9% of starting records.

stages.label: Matched and underwritten wrap files
stages.value: 12 files equal 26.7% of qualified opportunities
stages.detail: Each file has a specific qualified buyer, licensed RMLO review, documented repayment analysis, and counsel-reviewed structure. These files equal 2.4% of starting records.

stages.label: Funded and servicer-boarded wraps
stages.value: Six closings equal 50% of underwritten files
stages.detail: Count only executed closings with confirmed funding, recording submission, servicing setup, and an underlying payment schedule. Final conversion equals 1.2% of records.

diagrams.title: $475,000 Operator Revenue to $190,000 Owner Profit
diagrams.subtitle: Four expense deductions reconcile exactly to the Base-Case 40.0% net margin.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Annual USD. First and final bars are totals; intervening bars are signed deductions. Canonical revenue already excludes home face value and pass-through debt service. The four expense allocations are editorial assumptions totaling $285,000, not additional canonical inputs. Do not deduct senior debt twice.
diagrams.caption: Conservative: $100,000 revenue less $72,000 expenses equals $28,000 profit at 28%. Base: $475,000 less $285,000 equals $190,000 at 40.0%. Scaled: $850,000 less $408,000 equals $442,000 at 52%. Core staffing is four people; scaled staffing is six. These are annual scenarios, not month-one run rates.

stages.label: Gross operator revenue
stages.value: $475,000 annual retained-spread revenue before operating expenses
stages.detail: Illustratively, $210,000 earned net upfront spreads plus $265,000 retained annual wrap interest equals $475,000. Do not book every cash down payment as earned revenue. Apply transaction-specific accounting: interest follows applicable interest guidance, while any ASC 606 service component requires its own principal-versus-agent analysis.

stages.label: Acquisition and closing expenses
stages.value: Subtract $100,000 of annual direct transaction expenses
stages.detail: Allocate sourcing, title, recording, counsel, and transaction-specific origination expenses not already netted from upfront spreads. Running contribution becomes $375,000; property purchase principal is excluded.

stages.label: Realized losses and carrying expenses
stages.value: Subtract $80,000 of annual loss and workout expenses
stages.detail: Model recognized credit losses, property protection, workout counsel, and nonrecoverable carrying expenses. Running contribution becomes $295,000. Moving cash into a reserve account is not itself an expense.

stages.label: Contractor and servicing expenses
stages.value: Subtract $60,000 of annual recurring delivery expenses
stages.detail: Cover recurring contractor retainers, licensed servicing charges, reconciliation support, and borrower-service administration. Running contribution becomes $235,000; exclude origination charges already assigned above.

stages.label: Systems and administrative overhead
stages.value: Subtract $45,000 of annual recurring overhead expenses
stages.detail: Cover CRM, document controls, bookkeeping, business insurance, and administrative support. Combined with the prior $60,000, recurring overhead equals $105,000 annually, or $8,750 monthly, within the stated opex range.

stages.label: Annual owner net profit
stages.value: $190,000 remaining profit equals exactly 40.0% margin
stages.detail: Calculate $475,000 minus $100,000 minus $80,000 minus $60,000 minus $45,000. Owner distributions and personal taxes are outside this illustrative operating bridge; profit does not equal immediately distributable cash.

diagrams.title: Five Sub-Niches, One Consistent Spread Measure
diagrams.subtitle: Compare contractual rate-spread proxies, not borrower APR or investor return.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are annual percentage-point differences between illustrative wrap and underlying note rates. Rates are examples, not market quotes. Unequal balances, amortization, defaults, fees, escrow, and prepayments change actual retained yield.
diagrams.caption: At equal $100,000 interest-only balances, one percentage point equals $1,000 annual gross interest spread. Actual underwriting must model both amortization schedules and monthly cash timing.

stages.label: Clean-payment low-equity resale
stages.value: 3.0 percentage points from 6.5% less 3.5%
stages.detail: Illustrative equal-balance gross spread is $3,000 annually per $100,000. Use licensed-servicer ACH collections and verify senior-lender settlement rather than relying on a buyer payment screenshot.

stages.label: Relocation seller with seasoned debt
stages.value: 3.5 percentage points from 7.0% less 3.5%
stages.detail: Illustrative equal-balance gross spread is $3,500 annually per $100,000. Confirm occupancy and insurance changes, obtain a complete payment history, and model seller release separately from the property transfer.

stages.label: Documented reinstatement opportunity
stages.value: 4.0 percentage points from 7.5% less 3.5%
stages.detail: Illustrative equal-balance gross spread is $4,000 annually per $100,000. A higher spread can disappear after arrears, reinstatement fees, foreclosure deadlines, and a delayed first wrap payment.

stages.label: Self-employed owner-occupant buyer
stages.value: 4.5 percentage points from 8.0% less 3.5%
stages.detail: Illustrative equal-balance gross spread is $4,500 annually per $100,000. Require RMLO-reviewed income evidence and repayment capacity; a larger down payment does not replace the required underwriting analysis.

stages.label: Texas covered wrap transaction
stages.value: 5.0 percentage points from 8.5% less 3.5%
stages.detail: Illustrative equal-balance gross spread is $5,000 annually per $100,000. Price only after reviewing Texas Finance Code Chapter 159, Property Code §5.016, applicable rate limits, licensing, and required disclosures.

diagrams.title: Four Decisions Before Committing Capital
diagrams.subtitle: Each affirmative branch advances; each unresolved branch stops commitment.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The four nodes are sequential decision checks. Stage numbers represent order, not probabilities. Transaction scope, state requirements, lien terms, and borrower use determine the applicable rules; a servicer does not cure defective origination.
diagrams.caption: Do not conceal a transfer, substitute a trust label for statutory analysis, or infer lender permission from continued payment acceptance. Keep written evidence for every decision.

stages.label: Can acceleration be absorbed?
stages.value: Yes advances; absent funding means decline the acquisition
stages.detail: Review 12 U.S.C. §1701j-3 and the actual due-on-sale clause. Document lender permission where obtained or specific statutory protection where applicable. Otherwise quantify payoff exposure and verify available liquidity or a credible refinance plan.

stages.label: Is origination properly structured?
stages.value: Yes advances; deficient underwriting returns to licensed RMLO
stages.detail: Route every owner-occupant wrap buyer through a licensed RMLO. Map SAFE Act requirements under 12 U.S.C. §§5102–5103 and Regulation Z §§1026.36 and 1026.43. Document coverage, repayment capacity, compensation treatment, and any specifically applicable exemption.

stages.label: Are state wrap requirements satisfied?
stages.value: Yes advances; missing notices stop closing preparation
stages.detail: For Texas, counsel checks Property Code §5.016 for covered encumbered-property conveyances, including applicable advance notices, and Finance Code Chapter 159 for wrap licensing and transaction duties. Document recipient, delivery timing, closing conditions, and applicable exceptions rather than copying generic forms.

stages.label: Can title and payments remain controlled?
stages.value: Yes permits closing; unresolved control defects require remediation
stages.detail: Confirm lien priority, current taxes, insurance interests, and foreclosure remedies. Contract a licensed third-party servicer, document applicable Regulation X duties, test underlying-payment reporting, and fund transaction-specific reserves before accepting buyer funds.

diagrams.title: Four Core Seats, Six at Scaled Volume
diagrams.subtitle: One full-time owner and three contractors form the canonical starting pod.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each numeric value represents one person. Core seats total 1 FT + 3 C; adding both expansion seats produces 2 FT + 4 C. Title companies, lenders, and the servicer are external vendors, not extra dedicated pod seats. Contractor credentials must fit the actual duties assigned.
diagrams.caption: The owner controls capital and exceptions; the RMLO owns buyer underwriting; counsel owns transaction documents; servicing operations verifies the licensed servicer's payment evidence.

stages.label: Core owner and acquisition lead
stages.value: One full-time seat owns pricing and capital decisions
stages.detail: Maintain seller relationships, approve documented underwriting assumptions, manage acceleration liquidity, and review weekly pipeline aging. Personally resolve material exceptions rather than delegating risk acceptance to an automated CRM status.

stages.label: Core licensed RMLO
stages.value: One contractor seat owns buyer origination and underwriting
stages.detail: Collect repayment evidence, document applicable ability-to-repay analysis, manage required borrower disclosures, and coordinate permissible origination compensation. Reject incomplete files before the closing calendar creates pressure to bypass review.

stages.label: Core real estate counsel
stages.value: One contractor seat owns statutory analysis and documents
stages.detail: Review transfer restrictions, state wrap requirements, security instruments, remedies, and title exceptions. Coordinate external title and settlement vendors and maintain a transaction-specific notice evidence checklist.

stages.label: Core servicing operations specialist
stages.value: One contractor seat owns independent monthly payment reconciliation
stages.detail: Reconcile licensed-servicer reports against underlying lender statements and bank records. Track taxes, insurance, borrower inquiries, and delinquency aging; this seat does not substitute for required servicing licenses or external servicer functions.

stages.label: Scaled portfolio operations lead
stages.value: Second full-time seat adds capacity for portfolio exceptions
stages.detail: Add at scaled workload to manage reconciliations, collection escalation, servicer service levels, and cash forecasting. The owner retains capital decisions while this seat prevents exception queues from aging.

stages.label: Scaled diligence and coordination specialist
stages.value: Fourth contractor seat expands document and closing capacity
stages.detail: Collect authorized records, maintain title and insurance checklists, coordinate document delivery, and track closing dependencies. Leave regulated origination, legal interpretation, and licensed servicing activity with the appropriately credentialed providers.

diagrams.title: Allocate Startup Cash Before Buying Payment Spread
diagrams.subtitle: Four buckets reconcile to lean $12,000, planning $35,000, and expanded $65,000.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values show the $35,000 planning stack in USD. Every detail supplies corresponding lean and expanded allocations. These are setup-and-liquidity budgets, not property purchase prices, annual expenses, or a promise that acceleration can be funded from startup cash.
diagrams.caption: Lean total: $3,000 + $4,000 + $2,000 + $3,000 = $12,000. Planning total: $8,000 + $10,000 + $7,000 + $10,000 = $35,000. Expanded total: $15,000 + $20,000 + $10,000 + $20,000 = $65,000.

stages.label: Professional structure and document setup
stages.value: $8,000 planning allocation establishes transaction-specific operating documents
stages.detail: Lean $3,000; planning $8,000; expanded $15,000. Fund counsel review, RMLO engagement setup, entity records, state requirement mapping, and initial title diligence. Per-closing costs still require separate transaction budgets.

stages.label: Transaction and reinstatement liquidity
stages.value: $10,000 planning allocation supports documented closing cash requirements
stages.detail: Lean $4,000; planning $10,000; expanded $20,000. Hold cash for verified arrears, title cures, and closing timing differences. Decline deals whose cure requirements exceed committed funds; these amounts cannot fund an arbitrary senior-mortgage payoff.

stages.label: Sourcing and servicing infrastructure
stages.value: $7,000 planning allocation builds auditable records and payment rails
stages.detail: Lean $2,000; planning $7,000; expanded $10,000. Configure a CRM such as HubSpot, access-controlled document storage, licensed-servicer boarding, bookkeeping, and payment reconciliation exports. Use dual review for payment destination changes.

stages.label: Runway and exception cash reserve
stages.value: $10,000 planning allocation protects early operating continuity
stages.detail: Lean $3,000; planning $10,000; expanded $20,000. Preserve cash for operating delays and payment exceptions. At $2,000–$12,000 monthly opex, $10,000 covers roughly 0.83–5 months before transaction shocks; arrange more runway when the 2–6 month first-deal window requires it.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to a Documented Operating System
diagrams.subtitle: Build sourcing, underwriting, closing controls, and payment evidence before scaling.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Four milestone values are ending calendar days: 7, 14, 21, and 30. This sprint prepares the operation; the canonical first-deal expectation remains 2–6 months. Do not force a closing into thirty days to satisfy the diagram.
diagrams.caption: Day 30 success means an auditable acquisition and servicing process with named owners, funded operating runway, and a qualified pipeline—not an assumed funded transaction.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.value: Select the market and document statutory operating requirements
stages.detail: Owner and counsel choose one jurisdiction, review 12 U.S.C. §1701j-3 and applicable state wrap rules, engage the RMLO, and map title, disclosure, and servicing responsibilities. Deliver a written transaction checklist and startup cash allocation.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.value: Configure sourcing records and rehearse the underwriting workflow
stages.detail: Build the deduplicated seller cohort, configure CRM stage definitions, and assemble an authorized sample file. Test senior-debt amortization, wrap amortization, escrow changes, default carrying cost, and acceleration liquidity in a spreadsheet.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.value: Validate buyer qualification and licensed-servicer payment controls
stages.detail: Have the RMLO review a qualified buyer file when available; otherwise rehearse with clearly synthetic records. Confirm servicer licensing and contractual scope, test reconciliation exports without live funds, and rehearse a failed underlying payment escalation.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.value: Review qualified files and prove end-to-end exception handling
stages.detail: Counsel reviews candidate documents and notice timing; operations completes a mock monthly reconciliation. The owner verifies runway and deal-specific liquidity, records unresolved defects, and schedules only files that satisfy the documented requirements.
